title: The Lunceford vocal trio becomes a quartet
summary: Sy Oliver, Eddie Tompkins and Willie Smith had recorded "My Blue Heaven"; Young joined to make a quartet that did "Ain't She Sweet" and "Cheatin' on Me," while Dan Grissom sang ballads.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: He had a vocal trio in there before I came and they had recorded "Blue Heaven", which was a popular recording. And they did this before I came in the band.

That trio was Sy Oliver, Eddie Tompkins, and Willie Smith. And when I came in the band he made a quartet. He added me onto the trio, and they did a couple of things that became very popular. One was "Ain't She Sweet" and the other was "Cheating on Me". And --
But it says the Jimmy Lunceford Quartet or the Lunceford Quartet vocals --

Sy Oliver and Eddie Tompkins. Yeah, see, when I -- they were the trio all the time before I went in the band. Of course, Dan Grissom was the vocalist. And out of us four guys I don't think any of us could really sing. But we had styles -- a little style going and it really helped. But Dan Grissom was really the true vocalist with the group, you know. And he had a -- he sang very high -- he had a high pitch voice back in those days. But he had -- he sang most of
the ballads and things of that sort. All we did was the jump tunes and things like that, you know.
